input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 defaults all delivered Materials to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third-party) owned, with the Customer receiving only an internal-Enterprise licence and no right to modify. That reverses our position that we own deliverables created for us, with IBM retaining only pre-existing IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is only addressed as our responsibility at 11.6, and 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). Redline flips the default to Type I, extends the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and adds an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence to include modification, and confirm Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so Materials created during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned) rather than IBM-owned, and the licence to IBM's pre-existing Type II Materials embedded in deliverables should let us modify them for our business. We have also added a confirmation that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components, with no assignment or joint ownership; if IBM cannot move the default, our fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Materials for our business.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute, and prepare derivative works based on copies of Type II Materials, within Customer's Enterprise and for the operation of Customer's business.

ops.text: e. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers any such rights to IBM or creates any joint ownership of them.
